title: The Man Who Bought An Entire Bank For $1
sources: BBC History / Financial Times: The 1995 collapse of Barings Bank (founded 1762) after trader Nick Leeson lost £827M ($1.4 billion).
Bank of England / ING Groep Archive: ING acquired Barings Bank and all of its worldwide assets and liabilities for the nominal sum of £1.
The Guardian: Queen Elizabeth II kept accounts at Barings Bank; following the collapse and £1 acquisition, the bank was restructured and restored to profitability.

lines.text: This man bought an entire bank for one dollar.
lines.caps: This man | bought | an entire bank | for ONE DOLLAR.

lines.text: In 1995, Barings Bank was so prestigious,
lines.caps: In 1995, | Barings Bank | was so prestigious,

lines.text: even Queen Elizabeth kept her personal fortune there.
lines.caps: even | Queen Elizabeth | kept her money | there.

lines.text: Overnight, the royal vault was wiped clean.
lines.caps: Overnight, | the vault | was wiped | clean.

lines.text: Desperate regulators had forty-eight hours to find a buyer,
lines.caps: Desperate regulators | had 48 hours | to find a buyer,

lines.text: so an investor calmly stepped in,
lines.caps: so an investor | calmly | stepped in,

lines.text: slapped down a single one-dollar coin,
lines.caps: slapped down | a single | ONE-DOLLAR | coin,

lines.text: and took every vault, painting, and royal account.
lines.caps: and took | every vault, | painting, | and royal account.

lines.text: Within months, he turned it profitable again,
lines.caps: Within months, | he turned it | profitable again,

lines.text: proving the cheapest thing on Earth
